thread.title: Asian Stock Markets Retreat; Hong Kong and Shanghai Higher On Trade Outlook

author: MT Newswires
title: Asian Stock Markets Retreat; Hong Kong and Shanghai Higher On Trade Outlook

organizations.name: shanghai higher on trade outlook shutterstock

text:
Shutterstock photo Asian stock markets opened lower Tuesday on Wall Street cues and retreated on smartphone and tech-sector softness, but Hong Kong and Shanghai gained on reports that Chinese vice premier Liu He will visit Washington DC soon to prepare another round of Sino-US trade talks. In Sydney, traders complained that the Australian market, which fell 1.80%, has been "sold off on weak iPhone prospects."
In Tokyo, the Nikkei 225 opened lower on overnight Wall Street cues and could not regain ground, as the tech sector slipped despite a softer yen. Suppliers to Apple ( AAPL ) were hit on concerns the smartphone sector is too crowded. The Japanese currency fell to more than 114 to the greenback, regarded as a positive in export-oriented Japan.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 dropped 459.36, or 2.06%, to 21,810.52, as losing issues outnumbered gainers 214 to 11.
Leading the thin upside on a down day were CyberAgent (CYGIY, 4751:Tokyo), up 2.2%, followed by finance-tech shop SoftBank (SFTBY, 9984:Tokyo), up 1.9%, and then textile-house Toyobo (TYOBY, 3101:Tokyo), up 1.2%.
On the downside were engineering concern Taiyo Yuden (TYOYY, 6976:Tokyo), off 7.3%, and then Mitsui Mining & Smelting (MMSMY, 5706;Tokyo), off 6.6%.
The Bank of Japan now owns assets worth more than the country's annual GDP, following a half-decade of quantitative easing.
However, with Japan's consumer prices rising at about 1% annually, the Bank of Japan has yet to hit its 2% inflation target.
The Hong Kong Hang Seng opened lower on Wall Street cues and tech-sector softness, but rallied in the afternoon on the news of the pending trade-meeting between Washington and Beijing.
The broad gauge Hang Seng rose 159.69, or 0.62%, to 25,792.87.
Leading the upside were Geely Automotive (175:HK), up 4.7%, followed by Macau gaming-house Galaxy Entertainment (27:HK), up 3.2%, and then China Mengniu Daory (2319:HK), up 2.9%.
On the downside were oil drillers CNOOC (8831:HK), off 3.1%, and then PetroChina (857:HK), off 1.3%.
On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite rose 0.93% to 2,654.88.
China exports to the US are growing due to a strong American economy and consumer preference for Sino products, the state ministry of commerce said. The delivery of previously placed orders and front-loading by Chinese exporters also contributed to a robust performance in 2018.
On the other exchanges, the S. Korean Kospi declined 0.44%; the Taiwan TWSE fell 0.56%; the Singapore Straits Times Index lost 0.47%; but the Thai Set inclined 0.30%. In late trading in Mumbai, the Sensex was up 0.96%.
